newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Jan 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Jan 30.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on January 30. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Members of parliament have criticised South Korea's Kia Motors 67500.SK for not employing Indonesians at its plant in South Korea manufacturing Indonesia's "national" cars. The government has allowed PT Timor Putra Nasional, controlled by President Suharto's youngest son Hutomo Mandala Putra, to import 45,000 fully assembled cars from Kia Motors with special tax and tariff privileges for one year. The government has said the cars would be made by Indonesian workers in South Korea.

Forestry Minister Djamaludin Suryohadikusumo has confirmed that loans to state-run aircraft maker PT IPTN from interests on reforestation funds had been converted into government equity in the company.
Indonesia's largest noodle maker PT Indofood Sukses Makmur will acquire nine companies belonging to the Salim Group, which include four palm oil refineries.
Indonesia plans to launch a telecommunications satellite on board a Russian rocket next year to serve local cellular phone users. The satellite will be called "Garuda".

Indonesian conglomerate Bakrie & Brothers finally confirmed it had decided to sell its 49 percent stake in PT Indocopper Investama Corp, which has a 9.36 percent stake in PT Freeport Indonesia, operator of one of the world's largest copper and gold mines in Irian Jaya.
